messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Patient Name: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for the evaluation and treatment of left eye melanoma. After undergoing brachytherapy, the patient showed scleral thinning and uveal tissue prolapse at the site of the preexisting lesion. The patient underwent a block excision of sclera, ciliary melanoma, and adjacent iris tissue, which was performed through the opening of the sclera and was combined with a corneal tectonic graft.

Clinical Findings:
Upon admission, the patient was found to have a pigmented fusiform thickening of the iris root in the left eye. Gonioscopy revealed a well-circumscribed dome-shaped mass at the level of the ciliary body, between the 2:30 and 3 o'clock positions. UBM showed a medium internal reflectivity with an almost homogeneous acoustic structure. The lesion was classified as melanoma of the ciliary body, which involved the adjacent iris root. UBM also showed a local scleral extension of the tumor, which was under the conjunctival layer and 0.88 mm thick.

Treatment:
The patient underwent brachytherapy (106Ru) and received a total dose of 100 Gy at the apex, with a dose rate of 79.09 cGy/hr. The total dose at the sclera was 531.1 Gy, with a dose rate of 420.1 cGy/hr. The patient then underwent a radical block excision of sclera, ciliary melanoma, and adjacent iris tissue, combined with a corneal tectonic graft and 16 single stitches.

Histopathology:
Post-operative histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of spindle cell melanoma.

Follow-Up:
The patient had a BCVA of 20/20 at the time of discharge. The patient is recommended to have regular follow-up appointments with their healthcare provider to monitor their condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications:
[N/A]
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is a malignant melanoma of the ciliary body (spindle cell type) involving the adjacent iris root, treated with brachytherapy and then block excision. This is a malignant neoplasm, which falls in chapter C. Malignant neoplasm of the eye and adnexa is C69, and the ciliary body is C69.4. Melanoma of the eye is coded to C69 rather than to C43, which covers skin melanoma.

CODE: C69
